newsitem.title: USA: Donald Rumsfeld named chairman of Gilead.
newsitem.headline: Donald Rumsfeld named chairman of Gilead.

text.p: Former Defence Secretary Donald Rumsfeld will become chairman of Gilead Sciences Inc., effective immediately, the biotechnology company announced Friday.
Rumsfeld, 64, succeeds retiring chairman Michael Riordan. Rumsfeld joined Gilead as a director in 1988.

The Foster City, Calif.-based company specialises in drugs based on nucleotides, the building blocks of DNA. It makes Vistide, a drug approved last June for treating cytomegalovirus retinitis in AIDS patients, and is working on treatments for herpes in AIDS patients and other ailments.
Gilead's stock rose 75 cents to $25.25 in morning trading on the Nasdaq market.
Before joining Gilead, Rumsfeld was chief executive of Monsanto Co.'s pharmaceutical unit, G.D. Searle & Co.
He also sits on the boards of Gulfstream Aerospace Corp., Kellogg Co., Sears, Roebuck and Co., Tribune Co. and Swiss electrical engineering company ABB AB, Gilead said.
Riordan, who founded Gilead in 1987, will continue to serve as a board director, the company said.

Rumsfeld, secretary of defence and White House chief of staff under President Gerald Ford in the 1970s, also served four terms in Congress and was a former ambassador to NATO. He received the presidential Medal of Freedom in 1977.
